findings.title: Include identity type in denial cache keys
findings.body: The denial key uses the parsed subject ID but omits IdentityType, even though different identity types have different permission rules. For example, denying a dashboard read for `anonymous:0` caches a denial that also matches `render:0` for the same namespace, action, name and folder. The renderer is normally granted all dashboard reads, but now receives a denial until the cache entry expires. Include the identity type (or full subject) in this key to prevent one identity's denial from affecting another.

findings.title: Encode denial key components unambiguously
findings.body: Concatenating name and parent with underscores allows different resource checks to share a denial key. For the same namespace, user and action, name `a_b` with parent `c` produces the same key as name `a` with parent `b_c`; underscores are supported in dashboard and folder UIDs. A denial for the first resource therefore causes the second resource to be denied without checking its permissions, even if access is granted. Use an unambiguous encoding of the component tuple rather than delimiter concatenation.
